extracted.intended_audience: graduate students studying commutative algebra / algebraic geometry (exercise solutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Worked solutions and statements of standard results in commutative algebra/algebraic geometry (integral extensions, Spec maps, Noether normalization, Jacobson rings, localization). Targeted at students proving or applying these results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitive action of G on P and finiteness of P
rubrics_metrics.description: If G is a group of automorphisms acting on A and P is the set of primes in B lying over a fixed p in A, then G sends elements of P to elements of P, 1_G preserves q, composition axiom holds, and G acts transitively on P; moreover |P| = |G|/|Stab(q)| ≤ |G| < ∞ by orbit-stabilizer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: show σ(q) ∈ P for all σ ∈ G (integrality preserved), show existence γ with q ⊆ γ(q0) and use Corollary 5.9 to get equality; transitivity follows from group action on A; finiteness follows because the action has single orbit and orbit-stabilizer theorem applies. Use that automorphisms preserve primality and integrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois automorphisms preserve integral closure B and fixed ring equality A = B^G
rubrics_metrics.description: For any b ∈ B (integral closure of A in K), and σ ∈ G (automorphism fixing K ⊇ A), σ(b) is integral over A_G and hence lies in B, so σ(B) = B. Consequently B is stable under G and A = B^G (the fixed ring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses that integrality equations are preserved under automorphisms fixing coefficients; apply σ to the monic equation ∑ a_j b^j = 0 with a_n = 1. Use injectivity of field homomorphisms to deduce σ(B)=B and the fixed field relations to get A = B ∩ K = B^G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite fibers of Spec(B) → Spec(A) for integral closures in finite/separable/purely inseparable extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is the integral closure of A in L where L/K is algebraic (decomposed into separable and purely inseparable parts), then for each p ∈ Spec(A) the fiber {q ∈ Spec(B) : q ∩ A = p} is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle separable case by embedding L into a finite Galois extension L' and using the finite Galois group to bound fibers (apply Theorem 5.10, Exercises 5.13–5.14). For purely inseparable extensions, construct explicit bijection of primes by taking q' = {x ∈ B : x^{p^m} ∈ p for some m}, show q' is prime and unique over p, hence fibers are singletons. Combine to get finiteness for arbitrary algebraic L via decomposition into separable and purely inseparable parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXXIV: Homeomorphism of Spec(B) → Spec(A) in finite purely inseparable extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be an integrally closed domain with fraction field K and L a finite purely inseparable extension of K. Let B be the integral closure of A in L. Then the induced map f*: Spec(B) → Spec(A) is a homeomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: show f* is bijective (previous purely inseparable argument yields unique prime above each p and surjectivity) and continuous; apply Exercise 5.1 which says f* is closed when B is integral over A; a bijective continuous closed map is a homeomorphism. Conclude fibers are singletons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noether's normalization lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is a field and A ≠ 0 is a finitely generated k-algebra, then there exist y1,...,yr ∈ A algebraically independent over k such that A is integral over k[y1,...,yr].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof splits by whether k is infinite or finite. For k infinite: choose coordinates so that some subset x1,...,xr are algebraically independent and reduce number of generators by replacing xi with xi - λi x_n for suitable λ_i chosen using nonvanishing of the top homogeneous part; this yields integrality of x_n over the smaller subalgebra, then proceed by induction. For k finite: use a combinatorial trick replacing xi by xi - x_i^d with large d to ensure distinct exponents and obtain a monic polynomial in x_n over a subalgebra, then proceed by induction. Notes: the typical second statement (that y_i can be chosen as linear combinations) holds at least when k is infinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXXV: Polynomial function zero iff polynomial is zero (over infinite fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: A polynomial function g: k^n → k is the zero function if and only if g = 0 in k[x1,...,xn].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on n: for n=1 trivial. For n>1 write g as polynomial in xn with coefficients in k[x1,...,x_{n-1}]. Evaluate at xn=0 to deduce constant coefficient is zero function hence zero polynomial by induction; divide by xn and iterate to kill coefficients. This uses that k is infinite so nonzero polynomials cannot vanish on all of k^{n-1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak Nullstellensatz and maximal ideals over algebraically closed k
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is algebraically closed and A = k[t1,...,tn]/I(X) is coordinate ring of a variety X, then X ≠ ∅ (weak Nullstellensatz). Further, any maximal ideal m of k[t1,...,tn] has the form (t1-a1,...,tn-an) with ai ∈ k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence: Use Noether normalization to map X onto a positive-dimensional linear subspace of k^n, so X nonempty. For maximal ideals: show a maximal quotient field finite over k must equal k (since k is algebraically closed), produce the ai and then conjugate by translation automorphism to reduce to (t1,...,tn). Claim XXXVI gives the maximality check for ideals of the form (ti-ai).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXXVI: Ideal (t1 - a1, ..., tn - an) is maximal
rubrics_metrics.description: For any field k and elements a1,...,an ∈ k, the ideal (t1 - a1, ..., tn - an) in k[t1,...,tn] is maximal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: consider translation automorphism φ sending ti ↦ ti + ai; φ maps (t1 - a1,...,tn - an) to (t1,...,tn). The quotient by (t1,...,tn) is k (evaluation at 0), so original ideal is maximal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zariski's lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is a finitely generated algebra over a field k which is a field (or is an integral domain finitely generated as k-algebra), then B is a finite (algebraic) extension of k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: generate B by x1,...,xn. If n=1 derive algebraicity of x1. For n>1 reduce to case n−1 by viewing B as finitely generated over k(x1) and showing all remaining generators are integral over a localization Af, then argue integrality forces finiteness over k. Use that polynomial rings over fields are UFDs and integrally closed (Claim XXXVII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXXVII: UFDs are integrally closed
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a unique factorization domain (UFD) then A is integrally closed in its field of fractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: Write element a/b in lowest terms; if integral over A, clearing denominators yields an equation showing b divides a, contradiction unless b is a unit, so a/b ∈ A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma N: k[x]_f cannot be a nontrivial field for deg f > 0
rubrics_metrics.description: No polynomial ring k[x] admits f with positive degree such that the localization k[x]_f is a nontrivial field; if k[x]_f is a field then deg f = 0 and k[x]_f ≅ k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: if k[x]_f is a field and deg f > 0 then 1−f is invertible in k[x]_f so (1−f)^{-1} = g/f^m leads to contradiction modulo (1−f) showing k[x]_f/(1−f) ≅ 0 implying 1−f is unit in k[x], impossible since deg(1−f)>0 and k has no nonzero nilpotents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXXVIII: Localization preserves finiteness and finite generation
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is a finite (resp. finitely generated) A-algebra and S ⊆ A multiplicative, then S^{-1}B is a finite (resp. finitely generated) S^{-1}A-algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: finiteness as module: localize a finite generating set. For algebra generation: localize generators; write elements as polynomials with localized coefficients. Apply with S = A	extbackslash{0} to reduce to field of fractions and then apply Exercise 5.16 to get algebraically independent elements in S^{-1}B over K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extending homomorphisms through localizations and integral extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f: A → Ω and s ∈ A nonzero, f extends uniquely to f_s : A_s → Ω. If B_s is integral over A_s and f_s sends s to 0 in Ω, then f_s extends to g: B_s → Ω, and composing with the canonical map yields an extension φ: B → Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use universal property of localization to extend f. Then use integrality + Exercise 5.2 (extension through integral closures) to get g. Finally compose with canonical localization map h: B → B_s to obtain φ = g ∘ h.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXXIX: Subrings of algebraic field extensions containing base field are fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k be a field and Ω an algebraic extension of k. Any subring E with k ⊆ E ⊆ Ω is a field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take nonzero b ∈ E; b^{-1} ∈ Ω and is algebraic over k so satisfies a monic polynomial; multiply to express b^{-1} as k-linear combination of powers of b, which lie in E, hence b^{-1} ∈ E. Thus every nonzero element is a unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of Jacobson rings (equivalent conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several equivalent conditions for A to be a Jacobson ring: (a) every radical ideal equals intersection of maximal ideals containing it; (b) every prime ideal equals intersection of maximal ideals containing it; (c) for every integral domain quotient A' of A, intersection of maximal ideals of A' is zero (i.e., Jacobson radical zero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs: show implications between (a),(b),(c). Use that radical ideals are intersection of primes containing them; use homomorphic images to reduce to A/p; reference to EGA-equivalent formulations. These give practical tests for Jacobson property in rings arising in geometry/number theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XL: Homomorphic images of Jacobson rings are Jacobson
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Jacobson and B is a homomorphic image of A, then B is Jacobson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: for any prime p of B, consider B/p ≅ A/π^{-1}(p) and apply the Jacobson property to the quotient to get required intersection-of-maximals property; use Exercise 1.21 iv) and previous equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XLII: Maximal ideals correspond under integral extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ⊆ B is an integral extension of domains (B integral over A), then there is a 1-1 correspondence between maximal ideals of B and maximal ideals of A via contraction and extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: contraction of a maximal ideal of B is maximal in A (Corollary 5.8). Conversely, given maximal m ⊆ A, use Theorem 5.10 to find a prime q ⊆ B lying over m; show q must be maximal (otherwise a strictly larger maximal would contract to m leading to equality by Corollary 5.9), yielding bijection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XLIII: Contraction of nonzero ideal under integral extension is nonzero
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ⊆ B is integral and b ⊆ B is a nonzero ideal then b^c = b ∩ A is nonzero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: choose 0 ≠ β ∈ b which is integral over A with relation β^n + a_{n-1}β^{n-1} + ... + a_0 = 0; then a_0 = −(β^n + ... + a_1β) ∈ b ∩ A, so contraction nonzero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: Jacobson ring ↔ finiteness condition on finitely generated A-algebras that are fields
rubrics_metrics.description: A is Jacobson iff for every homomorphism f: A → B with B a field (or for every finitely generated A-algebra B that is a field), B is finite as an A-module (equivalently B is a finite A-algebra).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: (i)⇒(ii) use Jacobson property and Exercise 5.21 to extend maps and embed B into an algebraic closure of A/m to conclude finiteness of image; (ii)⇒(i) take B = A/p and argue using localizations B_f to produce nontrivial prime contractions unless A is Jacobson. This gives a practical finiteness test for Jacobson property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XLIV: Direct limit of local rings is local
rubrics_metrics.description: A direct limit (directed union) of local rings (with compatible inclusions) is local: its nonunits are the union of the maximal ideals of the constituent rings and this set is the unique maximal ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: show units in the limit are exactly elements not in the union of the maximal ideals (if x unit then x inverse appears in some subring); argue exactness of direct limits on short exact sequences and that the union of maximal ideals yields a maximal ideal of the limit. This is useful when constructing valuation rings via Zorn's lemma from chains of local subrings.
